clue.text: Tense, suffering from a hangover in the morning?

definitions.meaning: anxious and on edge, unable to relax

definitions.text: suffering from a hangover in the morning?
definitions.meaning: playfully read as two words: up (out of bed, as one is in the morning) and tight (drunk), though a hangover is really the morning after

explanation.surface: Someone nursing a hangover the morning after is edgy and fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: split the word as UP (risen for the morning) and TIGHT (slang for drunk).
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for nervously anxious, a direct synonym of tense.

clue.text: Ship one's breaking

definitions.meaning: a fast naval warship of a particular class
one who is breaking things, a wrecker

explanation.surface: A vessel is coming apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's breaking' reads as 'one is breaking', i.e. a person who smashes things.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a kind of warship, and literally anyone or anything that wrecks.

clue.text: Endlessly intertwine garland

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to wreathe is to twist or entwine together

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep weaving flowers into a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' removes the final E of WREATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring of flowers or leaves, the same thing as a garland.

clue.text: Unwanted delivery of boat, man reported

parts.note: a junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing boat

indicators.note: signals that we take how the next word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A boatman tells of some unwelcome post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' makes MALE (man) sound like MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unsolicited advertising pushed through the letterbox, post nobody wanted.

clue.text: Only kind pals who are not emotionally involved

parts.note: only means merely or just
kind means good-natured, good
pals are friends

explanation.surface: Describes caring friends who are nothing more than platonic.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said of a couple insisting there is no romance between them, only friendship.

clue.text: Tarzan, he is out of place in pilgrimage centre

indicators.note: these letters are displaced and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: The jungle hero looks incongruous among pilgrims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges the letters of TARZAN HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Galilee where Jesus grew up draws Christian pilgrims.

clue.text: Met an eccentric as intended

indicators.note: odd or irregular, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Meeting an oddball was deliberate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the letters of MET AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past participle of mean, to have as a purpose, so it equals intended.

clue.text: Complaint the compiler will head

parts.note: the setter speaks as I, and will contracts to 'll, giving I'll
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A grumble that the setter will deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves as 'the compiler', meaning I.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment or disorder, so it is a sickness.

clue.text: A soft fruit to come to light

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A mushy piece of fruit coming into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to become visible or emerge, the same as coming to light.

clue.text: See Liz in turmoil about rating, it's fairly large

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the next piece
in disarray, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a rating is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: Liz is upset about a sizeable rating score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turmoil' turns SEE LIZ into SIZELE; 'about' wraps that around AB. A rating is a naval rank sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizeable describes something of considerable size, decently big.

clue.text: Divert attention from Diane's pamphlet

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane, so Diane's gives Di's
a tract is a short pamphlet, usually religious or political

explanation.surface: Diane hands out leaflets to pull people away from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone is to draw their focus away elsewhere.

clue.text: Slightly sooner

definitions.meaning: preferably, as in 'I would sooner stay'

explanation.surface: Two adverbs placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means somewhat ('rather cold') and preferably ('I'd rather not').

clue.text: Train heard in nursery

parts.note: a child's word for a railway engine, imitating the noise a steam train makes

explanation.surface: A train can be heard from a children's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' points to the word being imitative of a steam engine, and 'nursery' to baby talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The childish name for a locomotive copies its puffing sound.

clue.text: Make public form in Excel

parts.note: to out something is to reveal or expose it
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a spreadsheet's table public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel' looks like the software, but it is the plain verb. In British schools a year group is a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to be far superior to them, to surpass them.

clue.text: Schoolmate not about could become abhorrent

indicators.note: the remaining letters are able to turn into a new arrangement
the next piece is missing from the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A classmate who drifts away from you could turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C (circa, about) from SCHOOLMATE, leaving SHOOLMATE; 'could become' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means arousing hatred or disgust, a synonym of abhorrent.

clue.text: Free policeman, powerless in pit

indicators.note: release these letters into a new order
lacking power, so the letter P, the physics symbol for power, is removed

explanation.surface: Release a helpless officer trapped in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' drops P from POLICEMAN, leaving OLICEMAN; 'Free' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a colliery, the excavation where coal is dug.

clue.text: Dandy follows celebrity to begin journey

indicators.note: the dandy's word comes after the celebrity's

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A fop trails behind a famous person as they set out.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to set out on a trip, to embark.

clue.text: Run up river as punishment

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Being made to run uphill beside a river as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TROT into TORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture is the infliction of severe pain, often as a cruel punishment.

clue.text: Conspicuous girl disheartened receiving a call

indicators.note: with the heart removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: receiving a call is getting a ring, a telephone call, here following the girl's remaining letters

explanation.surface: A downcast girl getting a phone call stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips the middle letters IR from GIRL; a ring is British slang for a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring means highly obvious, standing out so as to be impossible to miss.

clue.text: Letters exchanged before couple finally move

indicators.note: the scrambled piece comes ahead of the next
the letters swap places into a new order
take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pair swap letters before they finally relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges LETTERS into RESETTL; 'finally' gives E, the end of 'couple'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to establish oneself in a new home, i.e. relocate.

clue.text: Contribute in a flexible way

explanation.surface: Help out by being accommodating.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the adverb of supple, pronounced to rhyme with 'couple-y'.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply is to provide; and supply also means in a supple, pliant manner.

clue.text: Nonsense coming from motorist having stopped short and left

indicators.note: cut off before the end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a motorist is a driver

explanation.surface: A driver who braked suddenly and left spouts rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped short' drops the final R of DRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly talk, rubbish, a synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Caller does not have the item for part of helmet

indicators.note: the next piece is absent, so it is removed

parts.note: a caller is someone visiting, a visitor
it means the item referred to

explanation.surface: A telephone caller lacks a piece of headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caller' suggests a phone, but means someone who calls round at your house.
explanation.definitionFit: The visor is the movable front piece of a helmet protecting the face.

clue.text: Ancient city in display's a revelation

indicators.note: the city's name goes inside the other word

parts.note: to expose is to display; the 's stands for 'is' and links
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Seeing an ancient city on show is eye-opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "display's" stands for 'is', a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is the disclosure of something hidden, such as a scandal brought into the open.

clue.text: Doubt one working to follow hunt

indicators.note: the pieces for one working come after the hunt

parts.note: a quest is a search or hunt
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Someone at work has doubts about the chase ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To question something is to doubt it, and a question is a doubt.

clue.text: Plate of meat we hear Ian cooked

indicators.note: signals a word taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: lamb is a meat

indicators.note: the name's letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Ian has cooked a plate of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes LAMB sound like LAM; 'cooked' rearranges IAN into INA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or plate of material, such as bone or metal.

clue.text: Unrivalled lady about 50

indicators.note: the lady's title goes around the number

parts.note: a peeress is a woman of noble rank
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman of around fifty has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' but wraps PEERESS round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means having no equal, without match.
